attributes.title: Level 3

subgroups.name: Discover

steps.text: Watch this video to learn about using Boolean variables to control the conditions in a project.

questions.hint: Think about which values a Boolean variable can be set to.
questions.title: [Select one] How many different states can a Boolean variable have?
questions.correctResponse: A Boolean variable has only 2 possible states: true or false.

questions.hint: Notice where the NOT operators are used in each condition.
questions.title: [Select one] Which condition would check for a sprite that is jumping while moving left?
questions.correctResponse: The NOT operator checks if the sprite is not doing something, so this condition would run when the sprite is not walking right, but is jumping.

questions.hint: Think about where in the code a variable is initialized.
questions.title: [Select one] What does it mean to initialize a variable?

answers.text: To set its starting value at the beginning of the program
To change its value throughout the program
To reset the value when the function is called again
To shorten the name of the variable to only its initials

questions.correctResponse: Initializing a variable means to set its starting value at the beginning of the program, before it is updated by any functions or events.

questions.title: What different combinations of sprite states could you use in a project?
questions.correctResponse: There are lots of combinations of sprite states that can be used in a project, such as walking, running, jumping, and swimming. Be sure to use AND and OR operators when checking for different states in conditionals!

subgroups.title: Controlling Conditions with Boolean Variables
subgroups.introduction: Watch this video to learn about using Boolean variables to control the conditions in a project.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 3 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about using physics and Boolean values to control game conditions in 2D platform tilemap projects. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 3:

badges.title: Taking Control
badges.description: Control the way sprites move and appear on screen in a 2D tilemap project in JavaScript.

badges.title: Gravity of the Situation
badges.description: Use physics to control a sprite’s velocity and acceleration in a 2D tilemap project in JavaScript.

badges.title: Checkin’ it Twice
badges.description: Check for a specific tile image at a specific tilemap location.

badges.title: While You’re At It…
badges.description: Use a while loop to make something happen while a certain condition is true.

badges.title: And the Winner Is…
badges.description: Create a function that uses Boolean operators and values to determine which sprite image to use.

badges.title: Well-Rounded Character
badges.description: Edit an image asset to create multiple versions of an image that faces different directions.
